_comment: Custom seccomp profile for the Claude Code Workspace devcontainer.
It is INTENTIONALLY broader than Docker's default profile because the container
runs Docker-in-Docker (DinD), and Docker's default seccomp blocks several
syscalls dockerd needs to spawn nested containers (mount, unshare, setns,
The strategy here is denylist-first: defaultAction is ALLOW, with explicit
ERRNO entries for the exploit-class syscalls C-1 specifically calls out.
Concretely, this profile blocks: process memory inspection (when not using
SYS_PTRACE — which is no longer in --cap-add per H-1), kernel module loading,
kexec, BPF program loading, userfaultfd, and host-affecting calls like
reboot/swap*. dockerd's required syscalls are not affected.
This is honestly partial C-1 remediation: tighter than `unconfined`, looser
than Docker default. To move closer to default, derive from the upstream
Moby seccomp default profile and add only the DinD-specific exceptions.
Reference for the upstream profile: https://github.com/moby/moby (path moves
between releases; check the project's docs/ or daemon/ tree).

syscalls.comment: Kernel module loading — full kernel takeover primitives. Never legitimate from a container.
Load arbitrary kernel — would replace the running kernel; never legitimate from a container.
Affects the host. Should be capability-restricted but defense in depth.
Host swap manipulation. Container has no business doing this.
Known kernel exploit primitive (multiple CVEs). No legitimate container use.
Performance counter access — leakage primitive (Spectre-class side channels).
Filesystem handle operations — historical container escape primitives (CVE-2014-6271-class).
Cross-process memory inspection / injection. With CAP_SYS_PTRACE removed (H-1), these were less effective, but blocking them adds a hard floor.

Process attachment for memory/code inspection. CAP_SYS_PTRACE was removed (H-1), so most ptrace calls would already fail; explicit block here means even root inside the container cannot ptrace. If you need dlv / Go debugging back, re-add CAP_SYS_PTRACE in runArgs AND remove this entry.
Process personality manipulation — used to disable ASLR. Very rare legitimate use.
Direct hardware I/O port access. Kernel-internal primitives only.
